subject: history
title: Roaring Twenties, Crash and the New Deal
welcome_lead: Boom, bust and the federal transformation of FDR's New Deal.
meta_desc: AQA A-Level adventure on 1920s prosperity, the 1929 Crash, the Great Depression and Roosevelt's New Deal.
final_note: You can evaluate the causes and consequences of America's deepest economic crisis.

concepts.def: 1920s era of consumer prosperity, mass culture, jazz, automobile growth and stock speculation, alongside Prohibition and immigration restriction.
Stock market collapse 24-29 October 1929 (Black Thursday/Tuesday) wiping out around 25% of market value in days.
Economic catastrophe 1929-c.1939: unemployment peaked at ~25% (1933); 9,000 banks failed by 1933.
FDR's opening session of Congress (9 March-16 June 1933) passing 15 major laws including the Emergency Banking Act and AAA.
New Deal programmes such as CCC, TVA, WPA, NRA, SSA providing relief, recovery and reform.
Second New Deal law establishing federal old-age pensions, unemployment insurance and aid to dependent children.

walkthroughs.body_html: Republican presidents (Harding, Coolidge, Hoover) pursued tax cuts (Mellon), high tariffs (Fordney-McCumber 1922) and laissez-faire. Car ownership rose from 8 to 23 million. The 18th Amendment (Prohibition, 1920) was widely flouted; the 19th (1920) gave women the vote. The Immigration Act (1924) imposed national-origin quotas. Agriculture and the South remained depressed.

The Dow fell from 381 in September 1929 to 41 by 1932. Smoot-Hawley Tariff (1930) deepened the slump. By 1933, GDP had contracted by ~30% and one in four workers was unemployed. Hoover's Reconstruction Finance Corporation (1932) was too little. The Bonus Army march was dispersed in July 1932. FDR won the 1932 election in a landslide.

The Hundred Days brought the Emergency Banking Act, AAA, NIRA, TVA and CCC. The Second New Deal (1935) delivered the Social Security Act, Wagner Act (NLRA) and WPA. The Supreme Court struck down the NRA (Schechter, 1935) and AAA (Butler, 1936); FDR's 1937 court-packing plan failed. By 1939 unemployment remained at 17%; full recovery came only with rearmament.
